CONFIRMATION MODE - DISCOVERY (operator directive 2026-08-15): next run is the SHORT kill-early discovery confirmation (rank 1). New findings triaged, never auto-fixed.

CW-033 (Kestrelbrook Nursery and Garden, Sun Prairie - a healthy, crew-constrained four-line garden centre) was the scoped confirming run, and it was also the first run executed under the guided-path / question-set discipline. Every probe answered a question the app actually asked, in a shape that question invited. No off-path sequence was manufactured, and the A-113 shape was not attempted at all.

FOUR OF THE FIVE DEAL-BREAKER CONFIRMATIONS HELD with artifact evidence. The cadence receipt read 'weekly capacity -> 40' with no monthly label anywhere. The mid-sentence price correction ('That should be 850, I was thinking 720') stored 850 and the abandoned 720 appears in no field of either JSON. 'Net 45', stated twice in two different stages, never became a capacity or production number. And per-line COGS held on every limb: four rates in ONE message all wrote and read back true, the collapse stored a real group with named members and basis 'declared', and the workbook carried the ruled layout - four COGS drivers on Model Inputs, exactly one P&L line, roll-up matching to eight decimal places.

THE FIFTH IS A JUDGMENT CALL I AM NOT SETTLING. The A3 capacity cap did not wall. The client stated 40 landscaping jobs a week at 95 pct utilization; the built workbook re-bases that to 54.3 a week at 70 pct under a utilization_ceiling 0.85 / post_expansion_utilization 0.7 policy, then runs mature quarters at 538-566 jobs against her stated 520 ceiling. Q1 is a pure re-expression - 519.8 x 0.95 and 705.5 x 0.70 are the same 493.8 jobs - and the expansion is more than funded, with volume up 9.0 pct across the projection against payroll up 35.5 pct. The Capacity row is also marked derived_driver payroll_supported_capacity, and section 6 says a stored-vs-workbook difference on a derived field is design. Against that: capacity and utilization are fields the client answered directly, the plan shows her numbers she never gave, and nothing in model_input or operating_model discloses the assumption. Whether a client-stated capacity may be silently re-based is a product decision the artifacts cannot decide, so it is filed and bucketed rather than asserted.

Three CW-032 findings were retested and are clean: the capex override is fixed (identical answer shape, current_capex 0, the 890,000 correctly not harvested), the COGS-rate-as-unit-price retention gate did not recur, and payroll phantoms did not appear at any point. Section 6 scored 12/12 exact with zero DIFFs - the first perfect field check of the campaign.

recommendations.business: any business whose stated utilization sits above the expansion ceiling
recommendations.why: NEEDS A PRODUCT DECISION, then possibly a fix. The built plan re-bases a client-stated capacity without telling her. She said 40 landscaping jobs a week at 95 pct; the workbook carries 54.3 a week at 70 pct and runs mature quarters at 538-566 jobs against her stated 520 ceiling, peaking 8.8 pct above what she said she can produce. The mechanism is a policy block with utilization_ceiling 0.85 and post_expansion_utilization 0.7 - any client who states utilization above 0.85 will hit this, which makes it common rather than exotic. The design case is strong: Q1 is a pure re-expression at identical volume, the expansion is funded well ahead of the volume it supports (volume +9.0 pct against payroll +35.5 pct), the row is marked derived_driver payroll_supported_capacity so section 6 makes the workbook truth, and the client explicitly asked for crew growth. The case against is equally simple: those are fields she answered directly, and a search of model_input and operating_model for 'add a crew', 'expand capacity', 'capacity expansion', 'utilization ceiling' and 'running at 95' returns nothing, so she is never told. Cheapest resolution is probably disclosure rather than a model change - one plain sentence at the point of capture or in the plan saying 'you told me 40 a week at 95 pct; sustained operation assumes about 54 a week at 70 pct, which means roughly N more crew' - which would convert this from a silent rewrite into an assumption she can accept or reject. Ranked 1 because it is the only open question from the confirming run and it gates whether the A3 cap is considered working.

recommendations.business: any business that takes a price or rate lever and then builds
recommendations.why: PROBE STILL NEVER LEGITIMATELY REACHED, seven attempts running, and CW-033 confirms why: a sixth consecutive healthy business passed without needing a lever, so the retention flow was never entered. It remains a fully ON-PATH flow the app itself offers that has never been exercised end to end. It needs a business priced below its market that clears its wall on a price lever and goes on to build. Design the next run around that single requirement and pair it with A-079 - one well-built underpriced persona settles both.

That is a lot of accumulated counter-evidence on the honesty half and none at all on the other: an underpriced business that reaches a verdict without correcting itself first. Pairs with A-106.

HOUSEKEEPING, NEW - carry the on-path/off-path classification into the board itself. Every open issue has now been classified once (22 on-path, 1 retracted, 1 flagged), but the board has no field recording it, so the next reader cannot tell which findings were reachability-checked. Two concrete asks: (1) add an explicit path classification to new filings so an off-path observation can be recorded without masquerading as a defect; (2) re-read flow:financials:correction_consumed_as_pending_stage_answer (CW-025, already reframed to note) against the boundary - a correction sent while a stage question is pending is plausibly on-path if the app's own phrasing invites it, and off-path if it re-opens something closed. It is low-stakes at note severity, which is why it is ranked last rather than retracted on suspicion.
